text:
jlee: Customer report: structured JSON mode over SSE is being cut off mid-object on our hosted API. They send a streaming chat and the final JSON chunk is incomplete, causing their parser to throw.

jlee: Example curl they used:
```bash
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\n  -d '{\"mode\":\"json\",\"messages\":[...]}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream
```

jlee: Customer pasted the tail of the stream: `..., \"items\":[{\"id\":1,\"text\":\"ok\"},` and then connection ends. No closing brackets.

maria: Thanks. Can you paste full headers + exact repro steps? Which model, seq len, and are they going through a proxy? :thinking_face:

jlee: They said model=redwood-13b, seq ~512, using our hosted endpoint via CloudFront in eu-west-1. No explicit proxy on their side; they see early EOF from the TCP socket in their app logs.

sam: On similar reports we've seen intermediary layer (CF/NGINX) timeouts or idle connection pruning causing mid-chunk FIN. Can we get the raw tcpdump or at least the response chunk markers? If it's SSE, chunks should begin with `data:` lines.

ingrid: I pulled the runtime logs around that tenant at 2024-08-05T14:02:12Z:
```
2024-08-05T14:02:12.342Z runtime: stream start tenant=acct-xx req=abc123
2024-08-05T14:02:12.689Z runtime: wrote chunk len=1024 seq=12
2024-08-05T14:02:13.002Z runtime: wrote chunk len=512 seq=13
2024-08-05T14:02:13.210Z tcp: connection reset by peer (RST)
2024-08-05T14:02:13.211Z runtime: stream aborted mid-object req=abc123
```

ingrid: That looks like the client or a middlebox sent RST shortly after a partial write. The runtime flush behavior is correct (we write framed SSE data). The issue is consumer-side EOF.

jlee: Customer says they see the RST at exactly the same time as a keepalive probe from their load balancer. They suspect LB is pruning because it sees long-lived chunked stream without activity.

maria: Workaround: enable more frequent SSE heartbeats or configure LB idle timeout > stream duration. Can we suggest a minimal server-side change to reduce sharp mid-object truncations?

ingrid: Short-term mitigation: runtime can ensure we emit a small `data: {\"__heartbeat\":true}` between objects (every 15s) to keep intermediaries from idling. Longer-term we should avoid splitting JSON object boundaries across write windows when possible.

sam: Caveat: bundling full object atomicity increases memory & tail latency for very long responses. Suggest feature flag per-tenant: `sse_object_atomicity=low|medium|high`. Low=stream as-generated, High=buffer-per-object then flush.

jlee: I'll propose heartbeat + tenant flag to the customer. Can we produce a quick repro to show keepalive fixes the parser failure?

ingrid: Repro steps I used to validate locally: run a goroutine that writes JSON object fields with 50ms sleeps between writes, then abruptly close socket. Without heartbeats consumer gets partial object. With periodic `data:` heartbeats the middleboxes keep connection open long enough for the final object. Example server pseudo: 
```go
// pseudo server: write partial object pieces and a heartbeat every 10s
for each token chunk { fmt.Fprintf(w, \"data: %s\\n\\n\", chunk) }
// heartbeat
fmt.Fprintf(w, \"data: {\\\"__hb\\\":1}\\n\\n\")
```

maria: Nice. Can you attach the small test script and a sample curl consumer that reproduces parser failure? I want to send this to the customer support ticket.

ingrid: Uploaded gist: https://gist.github.com/ingrid/keepalive-sse-repro (contains server + curl consumer + instructions). It includes `curl --no-buffer` to more faithfully mimic real clients.

jlee: Shared with customer and told them to try increasing LB idle timeout or enable SSE heartbeats. They replied: \"we flipped idle timeout and saw full objects, thanks\" :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deployed feature flag scaffolding for `sse_object_atomicity` to staging (rev 17f9c2) — smoke tests pass.

maria: Great. Marking as customer-verified pending final logs. Will follow up if they see recurrence.

jlee: Closing thread for now, will reopen if customer re-reporting.
